title: Real or illusion?
hookLine: is the world real? two friends argue past midnight
carry: before judging the world, ask who is looking
tomorrow: every movie needs one thing nobody looks at. what is it?

lines: AN HOUR ON THE BACK STEPS.
cards: Two friends on the back steps, long past midnight. One has just watched a video: the world isn't real, it's all appearance. The other laughs: great, then pay my rent in appearance money.
They go around for an hour. Ramana's verses have a line for exactly this argument, and it isn't a point for either side.

teach.h: THREE, WHILE THE SEPARATE I LASTS.
teach.b: Just before it, the second verse of Ulladu Narpadu says teachings begin with three: the world, the soul and God. The one reality shows up as three, Ramana says, only while the separate I lasts.
Then the third verse, in paraphrase: the world is real; no, it's illusion. It's conscious; no, it isn't. It's happiness; no, it isn't.
What use is all this arguing? Set the world aside, know the self, and rest where there's no one and no two. He doesn't win the debate.
Every claim about the world is made by someone, so before settling what the world is, find out who's looking. That's Ramana's best-known practice, self-inquiry: asking, who am I?

teach.h: A WEEK OF PICTURES, ONE TURN.
teach.b: And that's the turn this whole week has made. A painted cloth under every figure. A tenth traveler who was doing the counting.
A glow that leads to the real jewel. A lamp, the witness, still burning in an empty hall. The great sayings, weighed word by word.

teach.h: FROM THE SEEN TO THE ONE SEEING.
teach.b: Different pictures, one turn: from the thing seen to the one seeing.

how: Ramana's followers read the verses slowly, often one at a time, and turn each one back on the reader with the question 'who am I?'

games.q: the week, back again — tap the pairs.

s: Ramana's verses say the world is just a dream
he sets the real-or-illusion quarrel aside and asks who's looking.
the second verse says the one reality appears as world, soul and God while the separate I lasts
with that I gone, what's left is resting in one's own being.
in the Panchadashi, the tenth traveler drowned in the river
nobody drowned; each counter left out himself.

games.q: two classmates argue whether free will is an illusion and want you to judge. what's Ramana's move?
o: step back and ask who's doing the judging.
pick whichever side has the better argument.
say both are right and change the subject.
games.why: the third verse lists the quarrels and asks what use they are: know the self first.

practice: Sit with your hands open on your knees or lap, palms up, as if setting something down. When a thought arrives carrying a verdict, this is real, this is pointless, let it rest in the open hands without arguing back.
Then notice who the verdict was for.
